title: Promoting Efficiency, Accountability, and Performance in Federal Contracting

enrichment.summary: This executive order requires federal agencies to prioritize using fixed-price contracts that reward performance and control costs rather than reimbursing contractors for expenses. Agencies must justify exceptions, seek to renegotiate large existing cost-reimbursement contracts, and report on contract types to promote efficiency, accountability, and better results in federal contracting.
potential_concerns: Mandating fixed-price contracts may increase financial risk for federal contractors, potentially disadvantaging smaller contractors or firms with limited capacity to absorb cost overruns.
The flexibility exemptions for R&D and emergency contracts may lead to inconsistent application across agencies, creating accountability gaps and potential cost overruns in those exceptions.

Efforts to renegotiate or restructure large, existing cost-reimbursement contracts could disrupt ongoing projects, causing delays or reduced quality, impacting federal contractors and their employees.

The increased administrative burden of justifying and reporting exceptions to fixed-price contracts may lead to slower procurement processes and increased costs for corporations and businesses engaged in federal contracting.
